content: World No Tobacco Day is an annual global event observed on May 31. It was established by the member states of the World Health Organization (WHO) in 1987. The purpose of this day is to raise worldwide awareness about the tobacco epidemic and the significant burden of preventable diseases and deaths caused by tobacco use. The initiative specifically aims to reduce the approximately 3.5 million deaths that occur each year due to tobacco-related health conditions. In 1987, the World Health Assembly adopted Resolution WHA40.38, which designated April 7, 1988, as the first World No-Smoking Day. Subsequently, in 1988, the World Health Assembly passed Resolution WHA42.19, which established May 31 as the annual date for the observance of World No Tobacco Day. This day serves as a reminder of the devastating health consequences of tobacco use, which contributes to the deaths of approximately 400,000 individuals globally each year.
